 Judgment

Appellant-injured has preferred this appeal against the Judgment and Award dated 21.08.2019 passed in MVC.No.230/2013 by the Civil Judge (Sr. Dn.) and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Koppal (for short, ('the Tribunal').
2. Parties herein are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Brief facts of the claim petition are that, on 22.08.2008 the petitioner was on her duty as a conductor in the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-37/F-134 and she went to Hospet.

sentences.text: That the petitioner again moved from Hospet in the above said bus and NC: 2023:KHC-D:11041-DB when bus was on NH-63 road, near Kirloskar Factory, there the offending Tipper bearing No.KA-35/A-2732 driven by the respondent No.1 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, dashed to the petitioner's vehicle and by the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries on her abdomen and on other parts of the body.

After the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Munirabad and from there she was referred to K.L.E. Hospital,
Belagavi for further treatment and there she was admitted as inpatient and from there she was admitted in Jude Doctor at Chikkodi as inpatient for a period of two months and spent Shalutai D/O. Dasharath Mugali vs Nagapane S/O.Neelappa Pande on 15 September, 2023

Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and doctor expenses, where the petitioner underwent various operations over the womb and ultimately the doctor found that the ovum (womb) was completely damaged due to the injuries and to save the life of the petitioner, the doctor removed the damaged ovum from the body of the petitioner.
Before the date of accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and maintaining her parents.
The petitioner has lost her womb in the said accident and she can never give birth to a child.

The very precious organ was NC:
2023:KHC-D:11041-DB damaged due to the injuries sustained in the above said accident and she lost her motherhood and by that nobody is coming forward to marry her and the petitioner leading miserable life.

The above accident has happened only due to negligent driving of the respondent No.1-driver of the offending vehicle Tipper bearing No.KA-37/A-2732 and respondent No.2 is the owner of the tipper and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the said vehicle.
Hence, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
On all these grounds, sought for allowing of the claim petition.
4. In pursuance of the notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are placed ex-parte.

In response to the notice,
respondent No.3 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement contending that respondent No.2-owner of the Tipper Lorry bearing No. KA-35/A-2732 has handed over his vehicle to the driver, who was having no valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle at the time of accident and the insured knowing fully well that the driver did not possess valid and effective driving license had entrusted the vehicle and thereby the owner has committed breach of insurance contract.

Further, it is contended that the alleged vehicle belongs to respondent NC:
2023:KHC-D:11041-DB No.2 was proceeding slowly and observing the traffic rules and alleged accident was happened not due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1 but same was happened due to rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-37/F-134.

The claimant has not made the owner and insurer of the vehicle i.e., KSRTC bus bearing No.
KA-37/F-134 as party, as such the petition is neither maintainable in law or on facts and it is liable to be rejected against this respondent.

The compensation claimed by the petitioner is too high,
inflated, unreasonable and without basis.
On all these grounds, south for dismissal of the petition with costs.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues;
(1) Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in an accident that occurred on 22.08.2008 at about 6:00 p.m. on Hospet-Koppal road NH-63, near Kirloskar Factory, Koppal,
due to rash and negligent driving of Tipper bearing No.KA-35/A-2732 by respondent No.1?
(2) Whether the respondent No.3 proves that driver of offending vehicle was not having NC:
2023:KHC-D:11041-DB effective and valid driving license as on the date of accident?
(3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
(4) What Order or award?

Issue No.1-In the affirmative.

Issue No.3-Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.4-As per final order.
8. In view of the above findings, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- with interest at 7% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant-injured has preferred this appeal for enhancement of compensation.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has awarded the meager compensation and has not considered the disability, future prospects and also period of taking treatment as inpatient.
On all these grounds sought for enhancement of compensation.

10. Learned counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal has awarded the just and proper compensation that there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned Judgment and Award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

11. Having heard the arguments and on perusal of the records, the following points would arise for our consideration:
(1) Whether the appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
(2) What order or award?

We answer the above points as under :
Point No.1- in partly affirmative Point No.2- as per the final order.

attendant charges and transport and Rs.25,000/-
towards medical expenses and Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities.
In all, Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: Issue No.3:- This issue is related to entitlement of compensation on account of injury sustained by the petitioner.

The petitioner who is examined as PW-1 has stated that she has sustained grievous injuries on her body and she also taken treatment at Government Hospital Munirabad and also taken treatment at KLE Hospital Belgaum and from there she was admitted to Jude Hospital at Chikkodi and she was in patient for 2 months and spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and doctor expenses and the petitioner underwent various operations over the womb and ultimately the doctor found that the womb was completely damaged due to the injuries and to save the life of the petitioner, the doctor removed the damaged ovum from the body of the petitioner.
In this regard the petitioner has produced Ex.P-7 wound certificate issued by Doctor Government Hospital Munirabad.
There are 5 injuries are mentioned in the said wound certificate.

According to the opinion of the doctor the injury No.1 to 5 mentioned are simple in nature and nowhere it is mentioned that the womb of the petitioner was damaged in the accident and said injuries are grievous in nature.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P-8, 9 are the radiological report and diagnostic report of the petitioner but on perusal of the said reports it is not clearly establishing that the injuries sustained by the petitioner to her womb is due to accidental injury.

Though she claimed she was referred to KLE hospital Belgaum and taken further treatment and she was in patient and also in patient in NC: 2023:KHC-D:11041-DB Judi doctor Chikkodi for 2 months and spent Rs.2,00,000/-
towards treatment.
Further, petitioner has not produced any in patient card or admission card and discharge summary which show that she was admitted to KLE hospital Belgaum and also Chikkodi hospital.

But she is relied upon the Ex.P-12 document issued by PW-2 which is the certificate issued by the Sri. Satya Sai Hospital Chikkodi by Dr. M.V. Musale but she has not produced any case sheet pertaining to any hospital and pertaining to discharge summary, admission card to show that she was admitted as in patient in Chikkodi hospital for 2 months and she underwent operation of womb.
Further petitioner has not established that her womb was damaged due to alleged accident.
The alleged accident was occurred on 22-08-2008.
As per Ex.P-7 nothing is shown that the injuries are grievous in nature but they are simple in nature.
According to petitioner she was admitted to Chikkodi hospital only on 18-06-2010 and abdominal surgery was done on 24-06-2010 and discharged on 03-07-2010.
Therefore, there are 2 years gap from the date of accident and surgery undergone by the petitioner.
Therefore, there is reasonable doubt arises regarding womb of petitioner was damaged due to the accident.
This Ex-P-12 document is not sufficient to hold that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

According to evidence of PW-2, who issued Ex.P-12 document, in his evidence he stated that she has admitted as in patient from 18-06-2010 to 03-07-2010 it clearly goes to show that she taken treatment as in patient for 15 days.

He also deposed that petitioner was informed that she has taken treatment for 2 days in Munirabad and 2 days in KLE hospital at Belgaum and has taken treatment for 2 months at Julde hospital at Chikkodi, but petitioner has not produced to show that she is admitted at Munirabad Hospital and KLE hospital and Chikkodi hospital.
In this regard absolutely there is not evidence on record.
Therefore, the evidence of PW-2 and Ex.P- 12 documents are not sufficient to hold that the injury sustained to her womb is due to accidental injuries and it may be caused due to some other reasons.
The petitioner has r produced any disability certificate and nowhere in Ex.P-12 stated about she has sustained 100% disability due to removal of womb and said fact is not mentioned in Ex.P-12.

Therefore, the grievous - 10 - Shalutai D/O. Dasharath Mugali vs Nagapane S/O.Neelappa Pande on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140587257/

sentences.text: 15. Further the petitioner has claimed in her petition the she was working as conductor in KSRTC bus during the time of accident and she has earned salary of Rs.15,000/- per month and maintaining her parents.
For that absolutely there is no material on record to show the exact income of the petitioner.
She has not produced any salary certificate, service register or any documents to show that she has been appointed in KSRTC as conductor and she has got monthly income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Except self-serving statement of PW-1 in her evidence no documentary evidence has been produced to show the income of the petitioner.
Therefore, under the above circumstances it is highly Impossible to ascertain the monthly income of the petitioner since she has not produced salary certificate from her appointing authority.
Further, as per Ex.P-12 she is admitted in Chikkodi Sri Satya Sai Hospital on 18-06-2010 and discharged on 03- 07-2010 it means nearly for 15 days she has taken treatment.

But already discussed above petitioner has not establishes that due to accidental injuries she has sustained grievous injury on her womb and she has underwent surgery and it is caused due to accident.
However the medical bills at Ex.P-10 goes to show that the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.6,823/-.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case this tribunal has assessed the compensation amount of the petitioner who has sustained injuries in the MV accident she is entitled for the following compensation:

Sl.No. Particulars Amount 1 Mental agony, pain and 50,000/-
 sufferings 2.

Medical expenses including 50,000/-
 food, nourishment, attendant  charges and transport 3. Future medical expenses 25,000/-
4. Loss of amenities 25,000/-
 Total 1,50,000/-
Therefore, under the above circumstances of the case, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11041-DB Rs.1,50,000/- from all heads.

The petitioner has produced certified copy of judgment and award passed in MVC.678/2008 before the Additional MACT and Fast Track Court-1 at Koppal dated 17. 07-2009 arising out of same accident in the case of death of KSRTC bus driver wherein the DL of the respondent No.1 is marked as Ex.P-10 and insurance policy of the offending lorry is marked as Ex.P-1 but in the present case on hand the petitioner has not produced DL or insurance policy.

sentences.text: Further, the respondent No.3 has not seriously disputed about the insurance policy hold by the respondent No.2 vehicle which was involved in the accident.
Therefore.
I am of the opinion that the respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest @ 7% pa.. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly.
I answer this Issue Partly in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: We have carefully examined entire evidence on record as well as medical evidence, we are of the opinion that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record and has rightly observed that the petitioner has not established that her voum (womb) was damaged due to alleged accident.

However, considering the nature of injuries, period of taking treatment as inpatient, pain and agony,
loss of amenities
, we are of the view that it is just and appropriate to award global compensation of Rs.50,000/- in addition to compensation awarded by the Tribunal without any interest.

Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following:
- 12 -  NC: 2023:KHC-D:11041-DB  ORDER  (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
 (ii) Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.50,000/= without any interest in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the above said amount within 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

If respondent No.3 has failed to deposit the same within 60 days, the petitioner is entitled for interest at 6% per annum over the global compensation from the date of this Judgment till its realization.

(iv) Draw decree accordingly.
